The *Koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadāna* is a verse text situated within the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali canon, catalogued under the reference Tha-Ap 427 [SuttaCentral]. Like other poems in the collection, it recounts the auspicious religious acts and past karmic aspirations of an elder (thera) named Koraṇḍapupphiya. SuttaCentral lists five modern translations of the poem across five different languages [SuttaCentral].

Computational text analysis by DharmaNexus reveals substantial Pali-internal text reuse, with 122 matching passages identified across 41 different Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Notably, the poem shares a virtually identical sequence of verses across its full extent (§0.2–12.1) with another poem in the collection bearing the exact same title, *Koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 495), with a match similarity of 0.99 [DharmaNexus]. Major portions of the text (§1.3–7.1) are also cited within the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus]. Recurring stock lines and formulaic verses, especially in sections §7–12, are widely shared with other apadāna texts, such as the *Kiṁsukapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 496), *Jātipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 460), *Paṭṭipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 461), and *Ekadīpiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 418) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus computes tentative cross-language alignments with Tibetan narrative texts, including the *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155-2) and the *Karmaśataka* (D0340), though these machine alignments do not constitute established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
